summary: Rewrote the overlay as a CS2-style translucent tint and the lot generator to fixed per-class dimensions. Fill is alpha 0.52 over the lit ground, so grass, wear and terrain relief read through it at every zoom (r1's blocker 1); the class colour is authored in display space and pre-inverted through AgX, so the eight palette hexes land on screen exactly instead of as AgX's pastel of them (r1 issue 8), and are driven by weather.night so 22:00 is a dim plan over a dark map (r1 issue 3). The 8 m lattice, the lot lines and the region outline are screen-space widths clamped to 1.0-2.5 px / 1.5-4.0 px, so they hold from 60 m to 660 m instead of vanishing at aerial (r1 issue 4). Overlay geometry is clipped against a new road-corridor field rather than against the cell lattice: the road-facing edge is the road's own offset curve at a constant 1.55 m from the paved corridor (frontEdge deviation 0.00 m over 174 runs), so nothing lands on asphalt, kerb or crosswalk (r1 blocker 2, issues 6-7). Lots are now exactly the spec's eight sizes, 142 of them over 1757 cells with 70.9 % of cells claimed and zero corner notches at 44 junctions. 32 gauntlet frames + 11 extra captures, all with zero console errors, 5 draw calls and 17.9k triangles attributable to the module.
remainingWeaknesses: Item 4: L22/L12 at the eight probe points is 0.51 / 0.32 / 0.54 / 0.44 / 0.43 / 0.27 / 0.62 / 0.72 - four of eight inside the required 0.35-0.55. The metric is (k*C - groundNight) / (C - groundDay) per class, so a single night multiplier cannot put all eight in the window when the eight class luminances (56-183) straddle the ground's (80-110): the low-density classes want k about 0.47-0.52 and the high-density ones about 0.55-0.65. k = 0.53 (with a 0.60 night fog relief) is the value that maximises compliance. See 'item4' below for the derivation.

Item 2: the closest of the 28 pair distances on crops_zones_12.png is commercial-low vs commercial-high at 37.2 against a floor of 40 (all 27 others clear it; the next lowest is 47). The palette separation is intact - those two hexes are 129 apart, 67 after the 0.52 alpha - the shortfall is that their two probe blocks sit on differently lit ground (one sunlit, one part-shaded), and the ground term does not cancel in a composited patch.

Item 3 aliasing clause: at zoneswide the on/off luminance-std ratio in the eight 100x100 probe crops is 1.02-2.07, and four exceed the 1.6 ceiling. This is added structure, not per-pixel static - the ratio rises because the lattice, lot lines and outlines are legible at 660 m, which item 5 requires. The static test that does separate the two, item 9's stipple count, passes: 0.05-1.08 % over crops inside a block against a 2 % ceiling.

Item 13's river-frontage run has 8 direction changes against a floor of 12. At seed 1337 the river bank only comes within the waterfront road's band over about 240 m of the district and the water severs the strip there, so the longest water-cut boundary run available is 20 cells. The hillside run is 57 cells with 30 direction changes.

Item 8's second clause (roads.isRoad === 0 at every frontEdge vertex) fails on 5077 of 5227 vertices, and cannot be met together with its first clause: roads rasterises coverage on a 4 m grid whose non-zero region reaches 4.0-4.5 m past the paved corridor, while the clause allows a setback of at most 2.0 m. Measured per type and filed as docs/core-requests/zoning.md item 2. The geometric clause holds exactly - clearance 1.55 m at every vertex on every type, deviation 0.00 m - and no vertex is on asphalt beyond the mask's own bleed (325 of 5227 read 1, all on 8 m alleys where the mask cell is wider than the road).

Item 16's fade timing is implemented (a linear ramp over 0.22 s of wall time, so 10 % -> 90 % is 0.176 s) but could not be demonstrated by sampling: at 1280x720 the ?showcase=all page renders at under 2 fps on this box, so a 25 ms sampler gets one sample per 700 ms and only ever sees 0 or 1. The group-toggle half of item 16 is clean: 0 draw calls and 0 triangles, twice in a row after the scene settles.

The overlay rebuild costs 47-60 ms for 1757 cells against a 45 ms budget (the band and lot passes are inside that; the geometry pass alone is 38-55 ms depending on machine load). The per-frame cost is unaffected - moduleMs is 0.0-0.4 in every shot.

cropRects' nearBlock cannot be at the 150 m the spec asks for: the declared zoneswide preset puts the camera 572 m above the ground, so the nearest painted block on screen is 583 m away. The two rects are the nearest and farthest painted blocks on screen (583 m and 862 m); api.cropDistances() reports what they came out at.
